entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Simon ben Boethos, a distinguished Jewish High Priest in Jerusalem during the late 1st century BCE, ascended to prominence through his familial ties to the Alexandrian Boethusian family and, critically, his daughter Mariamne's marriage to King Herod the Great. His tenure, roughly from 23 BCE to 5 BCE, was situated amidst the intense political machinations and shifting power dynamics of the Hasmonean-Herodian era, establishing him as a pivotal figure in the Roman-backed Herodian dynasty's efforts to consolidate control over Judea. His family's origins in Alexandria underscore the Hellenistic influences permeating Judean society and the interconnectedness of elite families across the wider Roman East.

Appointed High Priest by Herod around 23 BCE, Simon replaced Jesus ben Phiabi, a calculated move by the Idumean king to further embed himself within the Judean aristocracy and legitimize his reign through a new priestly lineage. His daughter, Mariamne II, became Herod's third wife, thereby significantly elevating the Boethusian family's status and providing Herod with an heir, Herod Philip I. This strategic marriage not only cemented Simon's position but also integrated his family into the very fabric of the ruling Herodian household, allowing them to exert considerable influence over religious and political affairs during a period of relative stability under Herod's firm hand.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Simon ben Boethos held the powerful office of High Priest during a critical period of Herodian rule, directly impacting the legitimacy and succession politics of the Herodian dynasty through his family's alliances. His career exemplifies the subordination of religious authority to political power in Roman Judea.
